Danger signs (IMCI): Gastrointestinal/circulatory: • Unable to eat or drink • Vomiting up everything • Signs of severe dehydration (sunken eyes, skin pinch returns very slowly) • Severe palmar pallor
Danger signs (ETAT): Gastrointestinal/circulatory: • Diarrhoea with any two signs of severe dehydration (lethargy, unconsciousness, sunken eyes, very slow return of skin after pinching) • Signs of shock (cold extremities with capillary refill time >3 seconds, weak and fast pulse)
Priority signs: • Any sick child aged <2 months • High fever (>39° C) • Severe pallor • Respiratory distress • Restless, continuously irritable, lethargic • SAM

Danger signs (ETAT): Respiratory: • Obstructed or absent breathing • Severe respiratory distress • Central cyanosis

Danger signs (IMCI): Neurological: • Seizures • Profoundly lethargic, unconscious • Neck stiffness or bulging fontanelle
Danger signs (ETAT): Neurological: • Coma (or seriously reduced level of consciousness) • Seizures
